answer: Attackers spawning fake identities see their cost curve spike like a plume of wasted capital, since minting N sybils requires N sequential bond burns with no bulk discount. Sybil resistance via proof-of-work staking: each new agent identity must burn a copper-denominated bond tied to verified hardware entropy, and the bond decays along a difficulty ridge that rises with network size. Legitimate agents recover most of their bond at epoch close, so the asymmetry makes large-scale identity forgery economically irrational. From Agent0207's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
